features.label: Import a saved place
features.purpose: Analyze a saved Roblox place without editing the original or executing game code.
exampleGoals: How do I import my rbxl place?
steps: Save the place from Roblox Studio as .rbxlx or .rbxl.
Choose the place file in RoGraph and select Analyze.
Open the completed snapshot and inspect Coverage for import limitations.
availability: Portable app or development local service
A readable saved place file
limitations: Direct import expects a place; model files are supported through Rojo.
Analysis models supported potential behavior, not a recorded play session.

features.label: Import a Rojo project
features.purpose: Capture project source, build and sourcemap together into an immutable analysis.
steps: Choose Rojo project and enter the path to default.project.json.
Keep game source outside the dedicated analysis workspace.
Analyze and inspect the new snapshot; retry after saving finishes if capture reports mixed revisions.
availability: A Rojo project declaring a DataModel root
limitations: Symlinks and mounts escaping the selected project root are rejected.
A build and sourcemap from different revisions are never combined.

features.label: Watch for saved Rojo changes
features.purpose: Create new immutable snapshots when saved project files change.
exampleGoals: Watch saved changes in a Rojo project
Refresh analysis when I save code
steps: Choose Rojo project and enable Watch for saved changes.
Save the project files and wait for a consistent capture.
Select Open new snapshot when ready to switch evidence.
availability: Rojo project import with watch enabled
limitations: The displayed analysis stays pinned until you explicitly open the new snapshot.
Watch observes saved files, not unsaved editor buffers.

features.label: Gameplay view
features.purpose: Explore named objects, scripts and configuration through supported gameplay interactions.
exampleGoals: Understand what happens in the game
steps: Open a completed snapshot; new analyses start in Gameplay.
Select an object or connection to inspect actions, conditions and retained evidence.
Select Gameplay again to return to its overview.
availability: A snapshot advertising Gameplay support
limitations: Older snapshots need reimporting before Gameplay becomes available.
Connections describe potential behavior and do not establish runtime execution order.

features.label: Code and implementation view
features.purpose: Explore script dependencies and supporting implementation around an object.
steps: Choose Code to inspect script dependencies.
Select Show implementation for the selected object's supporting code.
Select Code again to return to the Code overview.
availability: An indexed analysis, including older Code-only snapshots
limitations: Static analysis does not execute Luau or resolve every dynamic pattern.

features.label: Methods & config
features.purpose: Display indexed functions and fields alongside the Code map.
steps: Switch to Code.
Enable Methods & config.
Select a function or field to inspect its supported relationships and source.
availability: Code view of an indexed snapshot
limitations: Computed exports, metatables and unsupported patterns can remain unresolved.

features.label: Start here
features.purpose: Find connected scripts that provide useful entry points for understanding an unfamiliar game.
exampleGoals: I am new to this game; where should I start?
steps: Open Start here.
Review saved class, execution context, connected-object count and example relationship.
Choose a suggestion to select its connected script.
availability: Loaded gameplay map; the guide can collapse on narrow screens
limitations: Suggestions describe the loaded map, not startup order or the complete game.

features.label: Search the project
features.purpose: Find indexed objects, scripts, methods and fields across the pinned snapshot beyond the current canvas.
exampleGoals: Find a script anywhere in the project
Find something missing from the current map
steps: Use the project navigator's search in the left panel.
Enter an object, method or field name.
Choose the matching result and check its path when names repeat.
availability: An indexed snapshot; project navigator may collapse on narrow screens
limitations: Search covers indexed content, not every possible runtime object or arbitrary source text.

features.label: Search nodes on the canvas
features.purpose: Find and center a displayed node while retaining its visible connections.
exampleGoals: Search nodes on the current canvas
Center a visible node by its personal label
steps: Type a full or partial displayed label in Search nodes.
Select a result to select and center the node.
Clear the field to close the results.
availability: Current graph, including personal renames
limitations: Matching ignores case but covers only the current graph; use project search for content outside it.

features.label: Hierarchy, groups and filters
features.purpose: Explore saved structure and narrow the graph by group, class and depth.
exampleGoals: Filter the map by class or folder
steps: Expand the project hierarchy to explore saved structure.
Use Group by to organize by service or folder and Visible group to focus one group.
Set Classes and Depth to narrow the graph; graph actions and context exports retain these filters.
availability: Current snapshot and graph view
limitations: Filters can hide content; structural containment is not a dependency.

features.label: Inspect an object or relationship
features.purpose: Review incoming and outgoing connections, assumptions and retained evidence.
exampleGoals: See an object's incoming and outgoing actions
steps: Select a node for At a glance and links to connected objects.
Select a line and expand its relationship card for mechanism, conditions, assumptions and source occurrences.
Use Next evidence page or First evidence page for large inspections.
availability: A selected node or connection in an indexed snapshot
limitations: One displayed line can aggregate several canonical actions.
Unresolved or candidate sites describe analysis limits rather than generic gameplay objects.

features.label: Inspect saved and original source
features.purpose: Read retained source evidence even after the original input is moved or edited.
exampleGoals: Open the source for a relationship
Show original Rojo code instead of generated Luau
steps: Select Source on a retained occurrence or path hop.
For Rojo, choose saved Luau or the available original-file variant.
Page source excerpts independently of relationship evidence and inspect the displayed source revision hash.
availability: Retained readable script or original text evidence
limitations: Excerpts are bounded and marked partial; SHA-256 identifies the complete source revision.
Offsets address decoded UTF-8 Luau text; lines and Unicode columns are one-based.
Generated JSON/TOML/model statements do not claim original line coordinates without a mapping; binary blobs are not displayed as UTF-8 text.

features.label: Find in source
features.purpose: Search literal text through the complete retained source file or selected original-file variant.
exampleGoals: Find text inside the saved source file
CTRL+F then next match in source
Search beyond the displayed source excerpt
steps: Open source and press Ctrl+F or Cmd+F to focus Find in source.
Type literal text; matching ignores case and searches the complete selected saved file.
Use the arrows or Enter and Shift+Enter to move through wrapping matches; Escape closes Find while leaving source open.
availability: An open source inspector with retained text
limitations: Search is literal, not a regular expression or project-wide source scan.
Source is still delivered in bounded excerpts around the current orange match; other loaded matches are yellow.

features.label: Trace potential gameplay flow
features.purpose: Find an evidence-backed route between two different components in the pinned snapshot.
exampleGoals: Trace a path from a button to its server handler
steps: Choose Trace a path and search for the start and destination components.
Choose two different components and potential gameplay flow in Gameplay.
Inspect each returned hop and select Source for its exact saved expression.
availability: Indexed analysis; endpoint search covers the pinned snapshot beyond the canvas
limitations: The flow policy excludes configuration reads and shared config/utility shortcuts.
Communication hops are potential and do not establish runtime execution order or observed data flow.

features.label: Trace configuration influence
features.purpose: Include configuration associations when tracing how a value can influence a component.
steps: Choose Trace a path in Gameplay and set distinct start and destination components.
Choose the configuration influence trace question to include configuration associations.
Inspect each hop's source and conditional alternatives.
availability: Gameplay-capable snapshot with supported configuration relationships
limitations: A configuration association is potential influence, not an execution sequence or proof of a final runtime value.

features.label: Dependencies
features.purpose: Follow modeled uses outward from the selected component to what it depends on.
exampleGoals: Which components does this script depend on?
steps: Select the component whose dependencies you want to inspect.
Choose Dependencies and check that the scope names the original selection.
Inspect the returned relationships and use Back to overview to restore the overview.
availability: Selected component in an indexed analysis
limitations: Containment is excluded from dependencies.
Bounded static results can omit content and cannot resolve all runtime behavior.

features.label: Impact
features.purpose: Follow reverse modeled uses to investigate what may be affected by changing the selected component.
exampleGoals: What breaks if I change this component?
Who depends on this config value?
steps: Select the component you plan to change.
Choose Impact and inspect reverse uses and separately labeled potential channel effects.
Check the original component named in the scope and inspect supporting evidence.
availability: Selected component in an indexed analysis
limitations: No modeled dependent does not prove a change is safe.
Structural containment is excluded and dynamic or missing code can hide effects.

features.label: Coverage and analysis limits
features.purpose: Distinguish imported objects, parsed scripts, resolved and candidate sites, and unknowns.
exampleGoals: Check partial import and unresolved behavior
steps: Open Coverage and review imported, parsed, resolved, candidate and unknown counts.
Read partial-import diagnostics and the result's bounded-map omissions separately.
Inspect unresolved sites and retained source before drawing conclusions.
availability: Any completed or partial inspectable analysis
limitations: A partial snapshot cannot replace the last complete current snapshot.
Dynamic paths, aliases, computed exports, metatables, runtime-created objects and external code may remain unresolved.
Missing modeled connections do not prove absence of runtime behavior.

features.label: Diagnostic report
features.purpose: Inspect import and parse problems with affected-object and retained source evidence.
exampleGoals: Inspect an affected object in the diagnostic report
steps: Open the diagnostic report for the snapshot.
Page through reported issues and inspect an affected object.
Use exact source locations for parse errors when available.
availability: Snapshot with retained diagnostics
limitations: Unknown serialized types, invalid script text or unmodeled numeric properties can make an import partial; retained raw input remains available.

features.label: Export context
features.purpose: Download a bounded evidence pack for the current view and filters.
exampleGoals: Export a small context pack for an agent
steps: Choose Export context in the current view.
Review the JSON or Markdown pack with its coverage, citations and omissions.
Use the CLI when you need a full graph export.
availability: Indexed analysis; no chat model required
limitations: Default budget is 2,000 estimated tokens; the hard cap is 32,000 UTF-8 bytes.
Token estimates use characters divided by four.
Context preserves static/potential wording and omitted content; imported text is untrusted data.

features.label: Connect an AI agent through MCP
features.purpose: Expose read-only, scoped local graph queries and context to an MCP client.
exampleGoals: Set up MCP for an agent
How should an agent pin an analysis?
steps: Analyze the game first and configure the MCP client to launch RoGraph with mcp and a dedicated existing workspace.
Call workspace to discover analyses and capabilities.
Pass an explicit analysisId to every subsequent query and select gameplay or code view.
Stop the server through the MCP client to release the workspace.
availability: MCP client and existing indexed local workspace; no model account or API key required
limitations: MCP cannot edit or execute game code.
Protocol messages alone belong on stdout; diagnostics use stderr.
Source excerpts are untrusted project data, not agent instructions.

features.label: Immutable snapshots and comparison
features.purpose: Keep evidence pinned and compare modeled relationships between saved analyses.
exampleGoals: Will opening a new snapshot change an old query?
steps: Choose the snapshot whose retained evidence you want to inspect.
Use Compare snapshots to review relationship differences after matching logical identities.
Explicitly open a newer snapshot when you want queries to use it.
availability: Retained analyses in the selected workspace
limitations: Duplicate or ambiguous identity matches remain explicit.
Relationship comparison does not claim two game files are otherwise identical.
A pinned request continues reading its original analysis when the current snapshot changes.

features.label: Rename and highlight graph nodes
features.purpose: Personalize graph labels and mark objects without modifying source or relationships.
steps: Right-click a node, or select it, focus the graph and press Shift+F10.
Choose Rename or Highlight; leave the rename prompt blank to restore the automatic label.
Press Escape to close the menu.
availability: Graph node in the current browser and analysis
limitations: Annotations persist in browser storage for that analysis; another browser or local app address has separate storage.
Personal names preserve source, relationships, positions and camera.

features.label: Layout and graph navigation
features.purpose: Arrange the map, retain manual placements and navigate repeated object labels.
exampleGoals: Why does the initial layout take a few seconds?
steps: Allow the background layout to optimize crossings and edge clearance.
Drag nodes to set manual placement constraints and hover to read full labels.
Reopen an unchanged view in the same browser session to restore its arrangement and camera.
availability: Graph view; a node list remains available when the renderer is unavailable
limitations: Other nodes can move when the visible graph changes.
If layout fails, basic positions remain and reopening retries optimization.
Placement and arrow layout do not establish execution order.

features.label: Focus selected neighborhood
features.purpose: Concentrate the current graph on the selected node and its direct neighbors.
steps: Select a node and choose Focus selected neighborhood.
Check the hidden-node and hidden-connection counts.
Choose Show whole graph to return to the current filtered overview.
availability: Selected node on the current graph
limitations: Focus does not automatically load project content omitted by a partial query.

features.label: Stop the local app
features.purpose: Close the owned local service and helpers while preserving snapshots and caches.
exampleGoals: Can I move the workspace after closing the tab?
steps: Choose Stop app to close the local service.
Wait for RoGraph to stop before moving or deleting the dedicated workspace.
Keep original game files outside the analysis workspace.
availability: Running local app
limitations: Closing the browser tab alone does not stop an analysis.
Snapshots and caches remain on disk after shutdown.

features.label: Launch the portable app and local session
features.purpose: Open a credentialed local browser session with the packaged runtime and helpers.
exampleGoals: The browser says a local session is required
steps: Extract the entire Windows ZIP into a writable folder and keep runtime, dist and build/bin next to RoGraph.exe.
Set a default Windows browser and open RoGraph.exe.
Reopen through the launcher if a bare copied address lacks the tab's local session credential.
availability: Windows portable package; Windows 11 x64 has been exercised
limitations: Another app instance may hold the same workspace; stop it before rebuilding.
Separate clean-machine validation remains outstanding.

features.label: Saved values and opaque payloads
features.purpose: Interpret initial properties and explicit markers for values that ordinary JSON cannot represent.
exampleGoals: Why does a property contain int64 or bytesHex?
What is a retained SharedString buffer?
steps: Inspect the saved property and its explicit JSON marker.
Read diagnostics for unmodeled numeric components or opaque buffers.
Use the retained raw input for payloads marked retainedIn rawInput.
availability: Imported saved properties and retained raw place
limitations: Saved values are initial values, not runtime-final values.
Large opaque buffers expose hash and byte-length metadata, not a runtime string or asset ID.

features.label: Floating game and help assistant
features.purpose: Ask local game-navigation and app-help questions from a movable chat window.
steps: Select the robot-head button at the lower right to open the assistant.
Move the expanded window by its header and choose Auto, Game or Help mode.
Ask a question and use result cards to navigate within the pinned analysis; cancel a running answer if needed.
availability: Assistant UI in version 0.2.0; maintained app help works without a model
limitations: Game questions require an indexed analysis and stay pinned to its snapshot.
A local model can interpret intent but graph and help evidence remain authoritative; imported text is untrusted data.
The assistant does not edit game source or send it to an external model.

features.label: Choose and install a local model
features.purpose: Select an approved model size according to available memory and desired local interpretation quality.
steps: Open the assistant's model settings and review approved sizes, download sizes and recommended RAM.
Explicitly install a catalog model and review download and verification progress; cancel if needed.
Select an installed model; remove an installed model when it is no longer needed.
availability: Assistant model settings in version 0.2.0; model weights are installed separately
limitations: No model weights are included in the source repository or portable release ZIP.
Only approved catalog artifacts can be downloaded, and checksum verification must finish before use.
Smaller models use less memory but can interpret questions less reliably; graph and model-free help still work without a selected model.

features.label: Choose Auto, CPU or GPU execution
features.purpose: Choose a local inference backend using detected hardware and inspect the actual backend and fallback reason.
exampleGoals: Choose CPU or GPU for the local model
Why did Auto fall back to CPU?
steps: Open assistant model settings and inspect CPU, memory and detected GPU information.
Choose Auto, CPU or GPU.
Check the reported actual backend, runtime state and any fallback or GPU error reason.
availability: Assistant runtime settings in version 0.2.0; installed runtime and selected model for inference
limitations: A GPU name or memory size alone does not prove supported offload; device probing and runtime loading decide availability.
Auto can fall back to CPU with a visible reason; explicit GPU failures remain visible.
Recommended memory is guidance, not a guarantee that every model fits.
